problem: 2. Find the number of different ways to arrange all natural numbers from 1 to 9 inclusive in the cells of a 3 by 3 table, one number per cell, such that the sums of the numbers in each row and each column are equal. The table cannot be rotated or reflected.

# Finding Arrangements in a 3×3 Table with Equal Row and Column Sums

## Setting Up the Constraints

The sum of numbers 1 through 9 is **45**. Since all three rows must have equal sums, each row sums to 45/3 = **15**, and similarly each column sums to 15.

## Proving the Center Must Be 5

The four lines through the center (middle row, middle column, two diagonals) each sum to 15, giving a total of 60. The center cell is counted 4 times, while each of the other 8 cells is counted exactly once:

$$4 \cdot c_{22} + (45 - c_{22}) = 60 \implies 3c_{22} = 15 \implies c_{22} = 5$$

## Opposite-Cell Pair Constraints

Each line through the center gives a pair summing to 10:
- $a_{12} + a_{32} = 10$, $\quad a_{21} + a_{23} = 10$
- $a_{11} + a_{33} = 10$, $\quad a_{13} + a_{31} = 10$

The pairs from $\{1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9\}$ summing to 10 are: **(1,9), (2,8), (3,7), (4,6)**.

## Key Algebraic Constraints

Writing the grid as $\begin{pmatrix} a & b & c \\ d & 5 & e \\ f & g & h \end{pmatrix}$, the additional independent constraints are:
- **Row 1:** $a + b + c = 15$
- **Column 1:** $a + d + f = 15$ (with $f = 10 - c$) → $a + d - c = 5$, i.e., $d = c - a + 5$

## Systematic Enumeration

I check every valid choice of $a \in \{1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9\}$, then determine which $c$ makes $d = c-a+5$ fall in the correct remaining pair, and verify $b = 15 - a - c$ is in the last remaining pair:

| $a$ | $c$ | $d = c-a+5$ | $b = 15-a-c$ | Valid? |
|-----|-----|-------------|--------------|--------|
| 2 | 4 | 7 (P₃) | 9 (P₁) | ✓ |
| 2 | 6 | 9 (P₁) | 7 (P₃) | ✓ |
| 8 | 4 | 1 (P₁) | 3 (P₃) | ✓ |
| 8 | 6 | 3 (P₃) | 1 (P₁) | ✓ |
| 4 | 2 | 3 (P₃) | 9 (P₁) | ✓ |
| 4 | 8 | 9 (P₁) | 3 (P₃) | ✓ |
| 6 | 2 | 1 (P₁) | 7 (P₃) | ✓ |
| 6 | 8 | 7 (P₃) | 1 (P₁) | ✓ |

All other values of $a$ (1, 3, 7, 9) yield no valid solutions.

## Verifying the 8 Solutions

Each solution is verified (all rows and columns sum to 15):

$$\begin{pmatrix}2&9&4\\7&5&3\\6&1&8\end{pmatrix}\;\begin{pmatrix}2&7&6\\9&5&1\\4&3&8\end{pmatrix}\;\begin{pmatrix}8&3&4\\1&5&9\\6&7&2\end{pmatrix}\;\begin{pmatrix}8&1&6\\3&5&7\\4&9&2\end{pmatrix}$$

$$\begin{pmatrix}4&9&2\\3&5&7\\8&1&6\end{pmatrix}\;\begin{pmatrix}4&3&8\\9&5&1\\2&7&6\end{pmatrix}\;\begin{pmatrix}6&7&2\\1&5&9\\8&3&4\end{pmatrix}\;\begin{pmatrix}6&1&8\\7&5&3\\2&9&4\end{pmatrix}$$

## Symmetry Check

These 8 grids are exactly the **8 elements of the dihedral group D₄** (4 rotations × 2) applied to the single standard magic square:

$$\begin{pmatrix}8&1&6\\3&5&7\\4&9&2\end{pmatrix}$$

Since the problem states **the table cannot be rotated or reflected**, the grid is fixed in position, and each of the 8 distinct fillings is a **different** arrangement.

$$\boxed{8}$$
